pages.title: Introduction

frontmatter.title: Introduction
frontmatter.description: Get started with Grafana Advisor, find what to read next and learn which Grafana versions it needs.

pages.content:
Grafana Advisor runs regular health checks on your Grafana instance and recommends how to fix what it finds. Start with [Use Grafana Advisor](./grafana-advisor.md) to generate and read your first report, then use the other pages to tune which checks run and to automate Advisor with the CLI or alerts.

## Before you begin

Before you use the app, ensure you have:

- **Grafana permissions:** The `Admin` role. Only users with the `Admin` role can open the Advisor page and configure apps.
- **Grafana version:** Grafana 13.2 or later.

Grafana Advisor is enabled automatically when it's installed, so you don't need to enable it.

## Common tasks

- [Generate and read an Advisor report](./grafana-advisor.md)
- [Choose which checks Advisor runs](./configure.md)
- [Manage Advisor from the command line](./advisor-cli.md)
- [Get alerted when Advisor finds failures](./advisor-create-alert.md)
- [Fix errors in the app](./troubleshooting.md)

pages.title: Use Grafana Advisor

frontmatter.title: Use Grafana Advisor
frontmatter.description: Generate an Advisor report, understand each section and fix the issues it finds.

pages.content:
Grafana Advisor is a monitoring tool that helps administrators keep their Grafana instances running smoothly and securely. It runs automated health checks on data sources, plugins and the instance itself, and gives actionable recommendations. Open it from **Administration** > **Advisor**.

## Before you begin

- **Grafana permissions:** The `Admin` role.

## Generate your first report

To generate a report:

1. Log in to Grafana as a user with the `Admin` role.
1. Click **Administration** in the left-side menu.
1. Click **Advisor**.
1. If this is your first time, click **Generate report**.

After the first report, Advisor updates it periodically.

## Read the report

A report groups results into three sections:

- **Action needed:** Issues that require immediate attention. Each item shows the name of what needs fixing. For data sources, it shows the data source name.
- **Investigation needed:** Issues that don't require immediate action but deserve your attention, such as plugins that need an upgrade.
- **No action needed:** The checks Advisor ran and how many items it analyzed.

Each section is collapsible.

![The Advisor page showing an Action needed section with failed data source health checks](./img/advisor-report.png)

## Fix an issue

For each item under **Action needed**, one or more buttons appear:

- **Fix the issue.**
- The sparkle icon, which opens Grafana Assistant with the details of the issue. Refer to [Use Advisor with Grafana Assistant](#use-advisor-with-grafana-assistant).
- **Retry the check.**
- **Hide the error.** To show a hidden error again, click the **Hide/Show silenced errors** eye icon in the top-right corner.

To update plugins, refer to [Manage your plugins](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/plugin-management/#manage-your-plugins) for Grafana OSS and Enterprise, or [Find and use Grafana plugins](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/introduction/find-and-use-plugins/) for Grafana Cloud.

## Update plugins from the report

Items under **Investigation needed** work like those under **Action needed**. Click a plugin to open its upgrade page. There, update to the latest version or choose a specific version on the **Version history** tab.

## Use Advisor with Grafana Assistant

In Grafana Cloud, you can use Advisor with [Grafana Assistant](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/assistant/). Click the sparkle icon next to an issue to open a chat with the Assistant that already includes all the available information about the issue.

## Use the Advisor menu

The top-right corner of the Advisor page has these options:

- **Refresh** the report.
- **Configure application** (the cogwheel button) opens the app settings, where you can enable or disable checks. Refer to [Configure](./configure.md).
- **Hide/Show silenced issues.**
- **Delete reports.**

## Keep your instance healthy

To keep your Grafana instance reliable and secure:

- **Monitor regularly:** Check the Advisor page often to catch emerging issues.
- **Act on Action needed items promptly.**
- **Review systematically:** After you fix issues, click **Refresh** to confirm all checks pass.
- **Update proactively:** Address plugin update recommendations under **Investigation needed**, even if they haven't caused failures yet.

To get notified automatically, refer to [Create an alert based on Grafana Advisor results](./advisor-create-alert.md).

pages.title: Configure

frontmatter.title: Configure
frontmatter.description: Choose which Grafana Advisor checks run by enabling or disabling the steps of each check type.

pages.content:
Choose which checks Grafana Advisor runs by turning the steps of each check type on or off.

## Before you begin

Before you configure the app, ensure you have:

- **Grafana permissions:** The `Admin` role. Only users with the `Admin` role can configure apps.

## Open the configuration page

<!-- snippet:open-app-config -->

To open the Grafana Advisor configuration page:

1. Click **Administration** > **Plugins and data** > **Plugins** in the left-side menu.
1. Enter `Grafana Advisor` in the search bar.
1. Select **Grafana Advisor**.

<!-- /snippet:open-app-config -->

Then click the **Configuration** tab. You can also click the cogwheel button in the top-right corner of the Advisor page.

## Configure settings

The configuration page has no connection or credential settings. It lists the **Available Check Types** and lets you enable or disable each step of a check type. The available check types cover configuration, installed plugins and data sources, Grafana instance versions and SSO settings.

Each check type is shown as a card named **Check type: `<name>`**, with the following settings:

| Setting         | Description                                                                                                                                                  | Required |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| **Step switch** | Turns one step of the check type on or off. Advisor skips a step when its switch is off, so it no longer appears in the report. Every step is on by default. | No       |

Changes apply when you turn a step on or off. There's no separate save button.

> [!NOTE]
> If a card shows "Your current version of Grafana does not support ignoring steps", the switches are disabled. Upgrade Grafana to use them.

pages.title: Manage Advisor with the CLI

frontmatter.title: Manage Advisor with the CLI
frontmatter.description: Use the Grafana CLI, gcx, to list Advisor checks and failures, run checks and find plugins to update.

pages.content:
You can use `gcx`, the Grafana CLI, to manage Advisor `checks` and `checktypes` as resources. To install and configure it, refer to the [Grafana CLI documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/ai-tools/grafana-cli/).

## Before you begin

- **Grafana permissions:** The `Admin` role.
- **Tools:** `gcx`, configured for your Grafana instance, and [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/) for the JSON examples.

## Get the list of checks

To get the list of checks, run:

```bash
gcx resources get checks -o wide
```

For a more detailed view of the elements checked and failing, inspect the JSON output:

```bash
gcx resources get checks -o json | jq -r '
  ["TYPE","CHECKED","FAILURES"],
  (
    [.items[] | {
      type: .metadata.labels["advisor.grafana.app/type"],
      ts: .metadata.creationTimestamp,
      count: (.status.report.count // 0),
      failures: ((.status.report.failures // []) | length)
    }]
    | group_by(.type)
    | map(sort_by(.ts) | last)
    | sort_by(.type)
    | .[]
    | [.type, (.count | tostring), (.failures | tostring)]
  )
  | @tsv
' | column -t -s $'\t'
```

## Get the list of check types

To get the list of check types, run:

```bash
gcx resources get checktypes -o wide
```

## Show all failures across every check type

To see all failures in your instance, run:

```bash
gcx resources get checks -o json | jq -r '
  ["SEVERITY","ITEM","RULE","TYPE"],
  (
    [.items[] | {
      type: .metadata.labels["advisor.grafana.app/type"],
      ts: .metadata.creationTimestamp,
      failures: (.status.report.failures // [])
    }]
    | group_by(.type)
    | map(sort_by(.ts) | last)
    | map(select((.failures | length) > 0))
    | .[]
    | .type as $t
    | .failures[]
    | [.severity, .item, .stepID, $t]
  )
  | @tsv
' | column -t -s $'\t'
```

## Run checks for a type

To run the checks for a specific type, create the check resource and push it:

```bash
mkdir -p resources/Check/
echo '{
  "kind":"Check",
  "metadata":{
    "name":"check-manual",
    "labels":{"advisor.grafana.app/type":"<CHECK_TYPE>"},
    "namespace":"<NAMESPACE>"
  },
  "apiVersion":"advisor.grafana.app/v0alpha1",
  "spec":{"data":{}},
  "status":{
    "report":{
      "count":0,
      "failures":[]
    }
  }
}' > resources/Check/check-manual.json
gcx push checks/check-manual
```

Replace the following placeholders:

- _`<CHECK_TYPE>`_: The check type to run, for example `datasource`.
- _`<NAMESPACE>`_: The namespace of your Grafana instance, or `default` for self-managed instances.

Wait for the check to run, then read the results:

```bash
gcx resources get checks/check-manual -o json | jq '.status.report'
```

## Get plugins that need an update

To identify the plugins that need an update, run:

```bash
gcx resources get checks -o json | jq -r '
  ["PLUGIN","SEVERITY","PLUGIN PATH"],
  (
    [.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["advisor.grafana.app/type"] == "plugin")]
    | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last
    | .status.report.failures[]?
    | select(.stepID == "update")
    | [.item, .severity, (.links[0].url // "-")]
  )
  | @tsv
' | column -t -s $'\t'
```

## Find unhealthy data sources

To look for unhealthy data sources, run:

```bash
gcx resources get checks -o json | jq -r '
  ["DATASOURCE","SEVERITY","DATASOURCE PATH"],
  (
    [.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["advisor.grafana.app/type"] == "datasource")]
    | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp) | last
    | .status.report.failures[]?
    | select(.stepID == "health-check")
    | [.item, .severity, (.links[0].url // "-")]
  )
  | @tsv
' | column -t -s $'\t'
```

pages.title: Create an alert from Advisor results

frontmatter.title: Create an alert from Advisor results
frontmatter.description: Create a Grafana alert rule that fires when Grafana Advisor detects failures, using the Advisor HTTP API and the Infinity data source.

pages.content:
Create a Grafana alert rule that monitors Advisor check results and fires when Advisor detects failures.

## Before you begin

Before you create the alert, ensure you have:

- **Grafana permissions:** The `Admin` role, to create a service account and a data source, and permission to create alert rules.
- **Plugins:** The [Infinity data source](https://grafana.com/grafana/plugins/yesoreyeram-infinity-datasource/), version 3.3.0 or later, which supports the JQ parser used in this guide.

## Create a service account and token

Advisor results are available through the Advisor HTTP API. To query the API, create a service account and a token:

1. Click **Administration** > **Users and access** > **Service accounts** in the left-side menu.
1. Click **Add service account**.
1. Enter a name, for example `advisor-alert-service-account`.
1. Set the role to **Admin**, which gives the service account the required permissions.
1. Click **Create**.
1. In the service account details, click **Add service account token**.
1. Enter a token name and set an expiration date.
1. Click **Generate token**.

> [!CAUTION]
> Copy the token value immediately and store it securely. You can't view it again.

## Set up the Infinity data source

The Infinity data source queries the Advisor HTTP API using the service account token.

1. Click **Connections** > **Add new connection**.
1. Search for `Infinity`.
1. If the plugin isn't installed, click **Install** and wait for the installation to finish.
1. On the plugin page, click **Add new data source**.
1. Configure the data source:
   - **Name:** Enter a descriptive name, for example `Advisor API`.
   - **Auth type:** Select **Bearer Token**, then paste the service account token in **Auth details**.
   - **Allowed hosts:** Enter `https://<GRAFANA_HOST>` and click **Add**. Replace _`<GRAFANA_HOST>`_ with the host of your Grafana instance.
1. Click **Save & test** to verify the connection.

## Create the alert rule

1. Click **Alerting** > **Alert rules** in the left-side menu.
1. Click **New alert rule**.
1. Enter a rule name, for example `Advisor failures alert`.

### Configure the query

1. In **Data source**, select the Infinity data source you set up.
1. Configure the query settings:
   - **Type:** JSON
   - **Parser:** JQ
   - **Source:** URL
   - **Format:** Table
   - **Method:** GET
   - **URL:** `https://<GRAFANA_HOST>/apis/advisor.grafana.app/v0alpha1/namespaces/<NAMESPACE>/checks`

Replace the following placeholders in the URL:

- _`<GRAFANA_HOST>`_: The host of your Grafana instance.
- _`<NAMESPACE>`_: The namespace of your Grafana instance. To find it, refer to the [namespace API reference](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developer-resources/api-reference/http-api/apis/#namespace-namespace).

For more information about this endpoint, refer to the [Advisor HTTP API](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developer-resources/api-reference/http-api/advisor/).

### Configure parsing options

In **Rows/Root**, paste the following JQ expression:

```jq
.items | map({
  type: .metadata.labels["advisor.grafana.app/type"],
  creationTimestamp: .metadata.creationTimestamp,
  failuresCount: (.status.report.failures | length)
}) | group_by(.type) | map(sort_by(.creationTimestamp) | last)
```

This expression returns the most recent result for each check type, with its timestamp and failure count. You can use it to alert when any check type has more than 0 failures.

In **Columns**, add the following columns:

| Selector            | Format |
| ------------------- | ------ |
| `creationTimestamp` | Time   |
| `failuresCount`     | Number |
| `type`              | String |

### Filter by check type

Optionally, alert only on specific check types:

1. Go to the **Computed columns, Filter, Group by** section.
1. Add a **Filter**, for example `type == "license"`. Replace `license` with the check type you want to alert on.

### Set the alert condition

1. In **Alert condition**, select **WHEN Last OF QUERY Is above 0**. The alert fires when any check type has failures.
1. Click **Preview alert rule condition** to view the result of the query.

### Complete the alert configuration

Select your evaluation behavior, for example every 24 hours, and configure the notification settings.

## Save the alert rule

Click **Save** and verify that the alert fires as expected.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.content:
This page explains how to fix common issues when you use Grafana Advisor. For an overview of the app, refer to the [Introduction](./index.md).

## Configuration errors

These errors occur on the [configuration page](./configure.md).

### "Error loading check types"

**Symptoms:** The **Available Check Types** list doesn't load and the page shows "Error loading check types".

**Solutions:**

1. Reload the page.
1. Confirm you're signed in with the `Admin` role.
1. Open the browser developer tools and check the console and network requests for the failing Advisor API call.

### "No check types available"

**Symptoms:** The configuration page shows "No check types available".

**Solutions:**

1. Open the Advisor page and click **Refresh**, then reopen the configuration page.
1. Open the browser developer tools and check the console for Advisor API errors.

### "Your current version of Grafana does not support ignoring steps"

**Symptoms:** The step switches on the configuration page are disabled.

**Solutions:** Upgrade Grafana to a version that supports ignoring steps.

## Get more detail about an error

For errors in the app, open the developer tools in your browser and check the console.

## Get additional help

If this page doesn't solve your problem:

- Search the [Grafana community forums](https://community.grafana.com/).
- Open an issue in the [Grafana Advisor repository](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-advisor-app/issues).
- If your Grafana Cloud or Grafana Enterprise plan includes support, contact Grafana Support.

When you report an issue, include:

- The Grafana and plugin versions.
- The error message, with sensitive information removed.
- The steps to reproduce the issue.
- The app page where it happens and the relevant app settings.
